input: Get the gutters cleaned before the wet season

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The deadline is 'before the wet season' but the exact date matters — how much lead time exists determines urgency and whether a DIY approach is even viable.
Whether the user plans to do it themselves or hire a professional completely changes the plan — one requires finding a contractor, the other requires tools and safety prep.
The size and layout of the property (single-storey vs. multi-storey, total gutter length, presence of guards or leaf screens) determines complexity, cost, and safety requirements.
The current condition of the gutters — last cleaned date, known blockages, damage — affects whether this is a simple clean or also involves repairs.
If hiring out, knowing whether the user already has a preferred contractor or needs to find and vet one changes the immediate next steps significantly.
Does 'done well' mean just debris removed, or does it include a flush-through check, downpipe inspection, and a condition report? This scopes what to ask for.
Budget tolerance affects the choice between a budget service, a full-service company with inspection, or a DIY approach with rented equipment.

gold.taskTitle: Get gutters cleaned before wet season
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to arrange gutter cleaning on their property in time for the upcoming wet season.

questions.title: When exactly does your wet season typically begin?
questions.description: Pinning down the hard deadline — the specific month or date the wet season starts — determines how much time is available and how urgently to act.

questions.title: Will you hire a professional or do it yourself?
questions.description: This single decision splits the plan entirely — DIY means sourcing tools and safety gear, while hiring out means finding, comparing, and booking a contractor.

questions.title: How many storeys is the building and roughly how long are the gutters?
questions.description: The height and total gutter run determines the complexity, safety risk, and likely cost of the job.

questions.title: When were the gutters last cleaned, and are there known blockages?
questions.description: Recent history and current condition reveal whether this is a routine clean or a more intensive job that may also need repairs.

questions.title: Do you already have a contractor in mind, or need to find one?
questions.description: If a trusted tradesperson is already known, the next step is simply booking. If not, the plan must include researching, vetting, and comparing providers.

questions.title: Should the job include a downpipe and drainage check, or just debris removal?
questions.description: Clarifying what 'fully done' looks like — a basic scoop-and-go versus a flush test and condition report — scopes exactly what to request from a cleaner.

questions.title: Do you have a budget in mind for this job?
questions.description: A clear budget ceiling guides whether to choose a budget-only service, a premium full-inspection company, or to invest in DIY equipment.
